full_judgment: 11. Mr. A. B. Roy Chowdhury, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the learned Judge of the Single Bench of the High Court Division acted illegally and without considering the evidence on record discharged the Rule and that the petitioners are in possession of the suit land which has been proved by sufficient evidence. He further submits that the High Court Division failed to consider that the defendants totally failed to prove their title and possession by producing oral and documentary evidence and that the High Court Division failed to consider the scope of rule 95 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure which contemplates the eviction of the judgment-debtor and put the auction purchaser into possession and that there is nothing to effect partition for such auction purchased property, but all the Courts below including the High Court Division remained silent about the said fact. He further submits that the case of the petitioners is that exhibit No.' E' is a collusive document used by defendant No.1 and the same was not sustainable by the document itself as it was not signed by the Advocates of the parties and the High Court Division is totally wrong in not coining into definite findings on this point. He lastly submits that the Courts below and the High Court Division did not- consider that the possession is always delivered in accordance with sale certificate because the same is put into execution and presumption goes that the decree-holder auction purchased the suit property in equal share.
